s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic scrotal swelling with acute worsening and a palpable testicular mass
salient_findings: Firm, smooth testis without discrete nodules or tenderness
Hypoechoic lesion in the left testis with internal blood flow on ultrasound
key_facts: 20-year history of left testicular bloating and dull pain
Acute worsening of symptoms over the past 10 days
Left testis is enlarged, firm, and smooth
Transillumination of the left testis is negative
Scrotal Doppler ultrasound shows a hypoechoic lesion in the left testis
Internal blood flow is present in the hypoechoic lesion
Serum CA19-9 level is elevated at 57.5 U/mL
Alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin, and other tumor markers are within normal limits

shortlist.label: Seminoma
shortlist.why_kept: Most common testicular cancer, matches clinical presentation of a testicular mass

shortlist.label: Non-seminomatous germ cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Common testicular cancer, elevated CA19-9 level supports this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Testicular lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can present with testicular swelling and a palpable mass, rare but plausible

shortlist.label: Leydig cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause testicular enlargement and have variable tumor markers

shortlist.label: Testicular teratoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can present with a testicular mass and have elevated tumor markers

raw.rationale: The patient's 20-year history of testicular bloating and dull pain, along with the ultrasound findings of a well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion with internal blood flow and the absence of significantly elevated alpha-fetoprotein or human chorionic gonadotropin, suggests a Leydig cell tumor, which can present with long-standing testicular enlargement and have variable tumor marker elevations, including CA19-9.

rejected.label: Seminoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a shorter history and often has elevated human chorionic gonadotropin levels

rejected.label: Non-seminomatous germ cell tumor
rejected.why: Usually has elevated alpha-fetoprotein and/or human chorionic gonadotropin levels

rejected.label: Testicular lymphoma
rejected.why: More common in older men and often presents with systemic symptoms and rapidly progressive testicular enlargement

rejected.label: Testicular teratoma
rejected.why: May have a mix of solid and cystic components on ultrasound and often has elevated alpha-fetoprotein levels
